resources.string: Conversations
Talk with local models, then learn where llama.cpp servers and their saved sessions live.
AI Agent
Understand the agent workspace, its approval boundaries, and the controls that keep a long task recoverable.
Images and video
Choose the right local media tool, inspect its model and input requirements, and find the result afterward.
Voice
Move between speech, transcription, and translation while keeping model readiness and microphone state visible.
Documents
Review the document and dataset workspaces before committing files to a workflow or project.
Organizer
Keep notes, reminders, calendar views, and scheduled AI work in one predictable place.
Library
Find models, offline references, and retrieval knowledge bases, with clear readiness and recovery cues.
Infrastructure
Learn how local servers, distributed workers, benchmarks, terminals, and LAN sharing fit together.
Tama
Meet the companion room and its care, shop, farm, arcade, adventure, and gallery destinations.
Settings and help
Tune the app, identify the build, and read bounded diagnostics when something needs attention.

Chat is the conversation surface for a local language model. A configured, running llama.cpp server is needed for a response, but this lesson only asks you to inspect the screen. Use the server control in Chat to choose a running server or open server management. Settings → llama.cpp servers always opens the cards to create, configure, start or stop servers. The message composer and send icon create the conversation; the stop icon interrupts generation. If a server becomes unavailable, choose another running server or open its card to review logs and restart it.

Native Llama manages independent llama.cpp server cards, saved GENERAL commands, chat history, and scheduled runs. Its prerequisite is a saved command and compatible model path; neither needs to be started during this walkthrough. First inspect a server card, its port, and the play, stop, edit, and logs icons. The card reports stopped, loading, running, or error state and keeps session output bounded. If a port is occupied or a preset is missing, use Recover or edit the card after checking the displayed diagnostic.

AI Agent is the coding workspace for asking an agent to inspect files, plan changes, and run approved project work. A project folder and a configured local or remote backend are prerequisites; browsing the screen does not launch a task. First open the workspace controls and identify the robot, plan, approval, stop, and Continue actions. Results appear as bounded messages, file changes, and run status. If a tool call or connection is interrupted, the visible error state preserves a Continue path instead of silently abandoning the turn.

Image Generation groups Stable Diffusion create, image-to-image, inpaint, upscale, and gallery views in one workspace. You need a compatible model and a configured local backend before an image can be rendered. First inspect the task chips, model and settings gear, prompt area, and gallery tab; selecting a tab is safe and does not submit a job. A completed render is kept in the gallery with progress and failure details. If setup is incomplete, use the displayed environment or model status to return to configuration and retry later.

Video Generation exposes the Stable Diffusion video modes and their result gallery. A compatible video model, runtime, and enough storage are prerequisites, while this walkthrough only has you inspect the mode and gallery controls. First look at the create and gallery tabs, the prompt and input selectors, the settings gear, and the stop control. The screen reports preparation, frame progress, completion, or failure and keeps finished media in the gallery. When a backend or model is unavailable, read the diagnostic and return to environment setup before trying again.

ONNX Image Generation creates images with an on-device ONNX Runtime model. You need an imported or otherwise available ONNX image model and sufficient storage; the model page shows readiness without downloading anything here. First inspect the model status, image input or prompt fields, settings gear, and gallery or save controls. A successful result is previewed locally and can be revisited from the workspace. If the model is missing or incompatible, use the model-management link and its error detail, then return after the model reports ready.

ONNX Background Removal turns a selected picture into a transparent cutout using the configured ONNX pipeline. An image file and a ready background-removal model are the prerequisites. First identify the folder or image picker, the before-and-after preview, the model status, and the save or share icons; viewing those controls does not process a file. The result is a transparent PNG preview when the pipeline succeeds. If edges look wrong or the model is unavailable, choose another input or open model management and use the shown recovery message.

Video Upscaler improves video frames with the RealSR or RealCUGAN model pack and a selected scale or quality profile. You need a readable video, enough free storage, and the upscaler assets installed before processing can begin. First inspect the input file row, model or scale selector, settings gear, progress area, and stop button. The screen reports frame processing and the output location when complete. If the asset pack, file, or storage is invalid, the error panel explains which prerequisite to repair before returning to the same draft.

Video Interpolation uses RIFE to synthesize intermediate frames and make motion look smoother. A readable video, a compatible RIFE asset, and an intended output frame rate are prerequisites. First inspect the file picker, source and target FPS fields, scene-cut option, settings icon, and progress phases. The result is an encoded video with audio restoration when the pipeline finishes. If a frame or model step fails, use the diagnostic and keep the original input; correcting the file or rate lets you revisit the screen without losing the source.

Subtitle Burn permanently renders a subtitle track into a video with FFmpeg. You need a video, a supported subtitle file, and readable font or styling choices; the first visit only needs a review of those fields. Look for the video and subtitle pickers, font and placement controls, preview, and start or stop icons. Completion exposes the rendered file and its output status. If a subtitle parse or encoding step fails, keep the originals, read the log panel, correct the file or style, and return to the saved form.

ONNX Text to Speech turns typed text into local audio with an ONNX voice model. A compatible TTS model must be ready, and the screen can report that state before any text is submitted. First inspect the model selector, text field, speaker or rate controls, play, share, and gallery icons. A successful clip appears in the audio gallery and can be replayed without repeating the input. If the model is missing or audio playback fails, open model management or the gallery error detail, then return after the status is ready.

Live Translator provides turn-based bilingual speech translation rather than a continuous conversation transcript. You need microphone permission, a selected language pair, and the required speech models or backend. First inspect the source and target language controls, swap icon, microphone, speaker, and stop buttons; changing languages is safe for this tour. Each turn shows recognized speech and its translation. If capture or translation stops, use the visible permission or connection message, stop the turn, and reselect the language pair before speaking again.

Audio Transcription uses Whisper to turn an audio recording or selected file into editable text. A Whisper model and readable audio input are prerequisites, with model readiness shown in the setup card. First inspect the file or microphone picker, model selector, language and timestamp options, record, stop, and retry icons. A completed transcript offers copy and result actions while preserving the source. If decoding fails or the model is unavailable, read the bounded error, choose another file or model, and revisit the same draft.

Video Summary extracts audio, transcribes it with Whisper, asks the configured AI backend for a concise summary, and can save the result to Organizer notes. You need a video plus a usable Whisper model and summary backend. First inspect the file picker, model and backend indicators, staged progress steps, and note icon; do not start processing to understand the flow. A finished summary shows its transcript and save destination. If a stage fails, the progress panel names it, so you can correct that prerequisite and retry without replacing the source video.

PDF Toolbox combines PDF inspection, OCR, summarization, and related document actions. A readable PDF is the basic prerequisite; AI operations and the optional Llama OCR path also need their selected model or backend. First inspect the PDF picker, page preview, OCR, search, summary, and translation icons and switch tabs without submitting work. Results appear as extracted text or a bounded summary tied to the document. If a page or backend fails, keep the original PDF, read the page-level diagnostic, and retry the narrower operation after fixing its prerequisite.

Workflows chains supported document or media operations in a visible sequence, such as transcription, summary, or translation. Each step needs the input type and any model or backend it names; merely reviewing a workflow does not run it. First inspect the step list, input row, settings gear, progress markers, and per-step error area. A completed sequence exposes its outputs and the step that produced each one. If a step fails, fix that step\'s prerequisite and use its recovery control rather than rebuilding the entire sequence.

Dataset organizes source files into projects for training or fine-tuning preparation. A writable project location and compatible source documents are prerequisites; model or export choices are shown in the project screen. First inspect the project list, folder, add, settings, validation, and progress icons without creating a project. A project reports its file inventory, preprocessing state, and any generated artifact path. If validation finds a bad file or storage issue, open the project diagnostic, correct the source, and return to the same project instead of discarding it.

Organizer is the shared home for notes, calendar views, reminders, alarms, and saved AI results. No model is required to browse it, although scheduled AI actions need their own configured backend. First switch between the notes, calendar, and scheduled areas and identify the search, calendar, bell, edit, and delete icons. Existing entries show their saved state and next trigger. If a reminder or note looks wrong, open it from the list and use its edit or cancel control; the screen keeps the rest of the organizer available while a single item is repaired.

Knowledge manages user-owned retrieval knowledge bases: source documents become searchable chunks for later AI context. You need a readable source and a configured embedding server or model before indexing, but this lesson only reviews readiness. First inspect the base list, search icon, source and chunk counts, embedding status, and diagnostics card. A healthy base reports its indexed state and can be searched from the reader. If embedding is unavailable or a source failed, open the displayed diagnostic, correct the endpoint or file, and reindex that base rather than losing the originals.

Offline Library manages local ZIM archives through Kiwix and opens their pages without an internet connection. A compatible ZIM file and the Kiwix component are prerequisites; browsing the catalog does not require a download. First inspect the archive list, folder or storage icon, search control, and open-viewer action. A ready archive leads to a searchable offline page viewer and reports missing or incomplete files clearly. If an archive cannot open, check its path and component status, then return to the same entry after repair.

Model Library is the central hub for LLM, Stable Diffusion, ONNX, Whisper, TTS, LiteRT, and related runtime assets. Its first screen needs no model or network: it presents category cards and a local-storage note. First inspect the LLM, Stable Diffusion, ONNX, LiteRT, Whisper, and sharing cards and their memory, image, hub, voice, or share icons. Opening a card leads to the manager where location, readiness, import, and removal controls live. If an entry is invalid, use the displayed diagnostic in that manager and keep the original file.

AI Servers Hub groups the local web servers that expose configured AI tools over the device or LAN. A server\'s tool assets, port, and network permission must be ready before clients can connect. First inspect each card\'s address, status badge, globe, start, stop, and logs icons without changing its state. A running card shows the endpoint and a stopped card remains recoverable. If a port or process is unhealthy, use the card\'s log, stop, or start action, correct the reported conflict, and check the status again before sharing the endpoint.

Distributed LLM coordinates a llama.cpp master and workers so inference can use more than one device. You need reachable devices, compatible native binaries, matching model access, and a chosen master or worker role. First inspect the role cards, network diagram, worker list, layer or model settings, and play or stop icons; this reveals readiness without launching inference. A healthy setup reports connected workers and their contribution. If validation fails, follow the endpoint or capability diagnostic, repair one worker, and return to the topology screen.

Distributed Media sends Stable Diffusion media work through an RPC master and workers. Compatible media binaries, reachable devices, matching model availability, and enough shared storage are prerequisites. First inspect the master and worker cards, topology, model or device status, gallery, and stop controls without submitting a run. The workspace reports worker health and later associates output with the selected gallery. If a worker disconnects or a model is unsupported, use its diagnostic, remove the unhealthy participant from the plan, and revisit the configuration after repair.

Benchmark measures llama.cpp thread and model performance, with a history view for comparing previous runs. A usable native binary and model are prerequisites; the benchmark screen also explains thread and runtime choices. First inspect the preset controls, speed icon, model details, history tab, and cooldown status without starting a measurement. Completed runs show bounded metrics and remain in history. If a run is rejected or interrupted, wait for the cooldown message, read the diagnostic, and choose a smaller valid configuration before revisiting the benchmark.

Quadtrix is the native LLM training and runtime workspace with a Web UI card, worker card, and bounded monitor. A writable workspace and supported native binary are prerequisites; a dataset or checkpoint is needed only for training or conversion. First inspect the workspace picker, Web UI and worker endpoints, start or stop buttons, status badge, and copy or clear log controls without starting a process. The monitor reports tokenization, training, conversion, or worker state. If a process stops or errors, read the log and correct the workspace or endpoint before returning.

Termux connects the app to Termux or SSH-backed tools for terminal sessions, web surfaces, and file management. Termux, a reachable host, and any required saved tool configuration are prerequisites. First inspect the host card, connect, terminal, browser, folder, and file-manager icons without opening a shell command. A healthy connection exposes its session status and available files. If the host cannot be reached, use reconnect or the displayed endpoint check, correct the network or credential setting, and return to the same host card.

Ollama Manager keeps a local or remote Ollama endpoint and its model inventory visible. You need an Ollama service address and network access; the manager can inspect status without pulling a model. First review the endpoint field, connection test, cloud or server status, model list, and refresh icons. A healthy connection reports available models and service state. If the endpoint is refused or a model is missing, read the exact connection message, correct the host or service outside this lesson, and refresh the manager rather than repeating a failing request.

File Server shares selected device storage over the local network for another browser or device. Access to a folder selected in the system picker and a reachable Wi-Fi or LAN are prerequisites. First inspect the folder picker, running address, QR expand icon, and start or stop button without enabling the server. When active, the card shows its local URL and QR codes; stopping it closes the share. If folder permission is lost or the default port is busy, read the service status, choose a valid folder or free the port, and check the card before sharing again.
Room

The Tama room is the companion\'s home screen: it shows the current sprite, needs, mood, time, and shortcuts into the rest of the game. A saved profile gives the full room state; with no profile, this route shows first-pet setup instead of failing. First identify the pet status, heart or mood indicator, room controls, and navigation icons for care, shop, farm, and gallery. The room reflects saved state immediately. If a panel seems stale, use its refresh or return action and reopen the room before changing a care value.
Care and routines

Tama care balances hunger, energy, hygiene, affection, sleep, and daily routines from the main room. A saved pet supplies the current state; when no profile exists, the room first offers first-pet setup. First inspect the heart, food, bath, bed, and activity icons beside their status bars. Each completed care action updates the pet and can affect mood or growth. If an action is unavailable, follow the cooldown or needs message, let the state recover, and return through the room rather than repeating a disabled control.
Shop

The Tama shop is the farm supply store for seeds, tools, materials, upgrades, livestock, and selling eligible crops. A saved pet, current coin balance, and farm state are needed for transactions; the catalog can be inspected without buying. First look for the tab row, coin total, item cards, quantity controls, price labels, buy or sell button, and back arrow. Purchases update inventory or farm upgrades, while selling returns coins. If an action is disabled, read the balance, stock, durability, capacity, or placement message and return after the condition changes.
Farm

The Farm route is Tama\'s crop grid with watering, tools, upgrades, a well, composter, and optional planting or harvesting drones. A saved pet and farm state are prerequisites; decorations remain placeable in the main room even when a farm area is unavailable. First inspect the coin total, upgrade cards, tool sidebar, three-by-three tile grid, page arrows, and back arrow. Tiles show soil, crop stage, timer, and status; dialogs expose well, composter, and drone controls. If a tile is locked, dry, or invalid, follow its message and revisit it after the condition changes.
Arcade

Arcade is Tama\'s hub for two short games: a falling-object catch game and a memory game. A saved pet is required; opening the hub does not start a round. First inspect the game cards, preview panels, play buttons, left or right controls, score and reward labels, and back arrow. A finished round shows catches or matched cards, score, coins, and happiness reward, then offers replay or return to the hub. If input is unavailable or a round is interrupted, use restart or back to hub and preserve the saved pet state.
Adventures

Adventures opens Tama\'s battle gate for dream worlds, story phases, and RPG encounters. A saved pet, a battle profile or loadout, and unlocked phases are prerequisites; this lesson only surveys the gate. First identify the info button, world and phase choices, loadout or shop controls, battle status, reward panel, and back or retreat controls. A completed encounter records progress, XP, and rewards on the profile. If a phase is locked or a battle is interrupted, read the gate message, return to the room, and use the displayed retreat or recovery action.
Gallery

Tama Gallery collects saved companion artwork and daily-dream albums. A Tama profile and already-saved artwork are prerequisites for browsing; this lesson never requests generation. First inspect the gallery list, image or album cards, share and delete buttons, detail preview, and back arrow. A selected entry opens a preview with its date or story metadata; existing files remain separate from room state. If a file is missing or cannot render, read the entry status, keep other cards untouched, and return to the list after the file is restored.
Settings

Settings is the app-wide hub for appearance, language, AI behavior, storage, notifications, and feature-specific configuration. No model or server is required to read it. First scan the grouped cards and identify the theme, toggle, slider, reset, and back icons; each section explains its scope before a value changes. Saved settings apply to the related screen and survive navigation. If a choice causes an unexpected result, reopen the same section, restore the previous value, and use the displayed reset or defaults action when available.
About

About identifies the installed build, developer, open-source libraries, compatible tools, and support links. It has no runtime prerequisite and is safe to open when a feature is unavailable. First inspect the version row, library cards, GitHub or project link, support icons, and back arrow. The version and native build information help match a report to the exact app package. If a link cannot open, copy the visible version details, return with the back action, and use the device browser or the app\'s other help path.
Diagnostics and logs

Diagnostics opens the bounded logs and status views used to understand server, media, agent, and device failures. No active job is required; recent metadata and readable errors are enough. First inspect the filter, refresh, copy, export, and clear icons and the distinction between a log entry and a live status card. Results remain constrained so long output does not hide recovery controls. If a failure is visible, preserve the relevant timestamp and error class, use Continue or Retry on the owning screen, and clear logs only after saving what you need.
